basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A typed, attributable link from a citing context to a cited source with a precise locator.
Never restates or caches the cited content as authoritative.
Unlike a bibliographic record, it does not describe the work as a publication.
Unlike a claim, it carries no truth status of its own.

may: Mint a citation record and resolve its locator.
Anchor an excerpt within licence limits.
Re-verify a citation and detect drift in the cited source.
Classify the evidential link and assess certainty.
mustNot: Fabricate a citation or a locator.
Store excerpts beyond licence or privacy limits.
Present generated citations without marking the method, tool and model version.
Treat cited content as authoritative copy.
Claim conformance without a dated test result.
requiresHuman: Resolving disputes over whether a source supports a claim.

considerations: Fabricated or wrong citations mislead readers and damage trust in research.
Authors' copyright and moral rights must be respected in excerpts.
Cited personal material may need privacy protection.

items: A citation has a citing context, a cited source identifier, a locator and a link type.
Often confused with a bibliography entry, a claim, a hyperlink and a web archive capture.
Link rot changing what a citation points to.
